**Job description**
-------------------

The Implementation Engineer is responsible for end-to-end technical deployment, integration, and validation of Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) and related DeepHealth imaging solutions at hospitals and other healthcare facilities. This role partners with clinical and technical stakeholders, including radiologists, radiology administrators, clinical staff, network engineers, and third-party vendors, to deliver successful implementations with reliable DICOM workflows and enterprise imaging connectivity.

**Job requirements**
--------------------

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Serve as the primary implementation resource for assigned client projects from kick-off through completion.
* Coordinate project tasks and own delivery milestones while acting as a primary point of contact for customer communication and issue resolution.
* Deploy, integrate, and validate PACS and related imaging solutions in customer environments, including DICOM workflow and enterprise imaging connectivity.
* Provide second-level technical support for healthcare IT systems, including troubleshooting and resolving escalated issues during and after implementation.
* Collaborate with IT, Product, and Engineering to escalate and resolve complex technical problems.

Proven IT support experience, preferably in healthcare or clinical environments (required).

Hands-on experience with PC and server platforms and command-line administration on Linux and Windows (required).

Proficiency with Windows client and server operating systems and Linux system administration (required).

Strong networking and general IT skills, with experience troubleshooting complex applications and software products (required).

Experience with ticketing systems and ITIL-based support processes (required).

PACS, radiology workflow, DICOM, and/or HL7 experience (required).

Familiarity with healthcare IT systems, including EMR and clinical software (required).

Strong customer relationship skills and clear written and verbal communication (required).

Ability to manage multiple tasks, work under pressure, and collaborate across teams (required).

Flexibility to work varied hours and participate in on-call rotations (required).

Preferred: Knowledge of archival and storage media.

Preferred: CompTIA Linux, RHCA, RHCT, CCNA, or CCNP certification.

Preferred: Public cloud application troubleshooting experience (preferably GCP).

Preferred: Deployment and configuration automation experience (for example, Ansible).

**Meet Instinct**

Instinct Science is at the forefront of veterinary innovation, comprised of world-class tools that have served our industry for decades: easy-to-use veterinary practice software (Instinct EMR), an essential resource for expanding your knowledge and skills (Clinician's Brief), clinical and pharmaceutical decision support (Standards of Care & Plumb's), and an AI scribing platform (ScribbleVet). Combined, Instinct Science offers an ecosystem that veterinarians rely on for every aspect and stage of their careers.

At Instinct Science, we believe in leading with compassion. Our team, our customers, and their patients and clients are the foundation of everything we do. Our culture is guided by our U.C.A.R.E. values: We move fast because our mission matters, we put customers at the center of every decision, and we treat each other with kindness and high standards.

**A Sneak Peek of Your Role**

This is a fully remote role.

The Customer Implementation Specialist is a heads-down expert responsible for all data work that enables new hospitals to go live on Instinct. This role exists to move data projects forward with speed and precision — ensuring accurate migration of patient and hospital records, coordinating closely with the Medical Review and Data Migration teams, and meeting the turnaround SLAs that keep onboarding timelines on track.

Because this is your singular focus, you will move faster and more accurately than in any generalist onboarding role. You take pride in getting the details right — and you think about how technology can make that work better, safer, and more efficient. Patient safety is always top of mind: the data you work with goes directly into clinical environments, and you treat that responsibility seriously.

**Technology & Process Improvement**

jobs.description:
**Team:** Implementation, Logis · **Level:** Senior Implementation Consultant · **Reports to:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch) · **Location:** Remote, United States

**Outcome.** Dispatch centers go live on Logis Dispatch on the planned date, right the first time, and trust the system from the first call.

**About the role**

A dispatch center cannot stop to go live. When we implement Logis Dispatch, we change the system a center uses to send help to every call, on a floor that runs 24 hours a day. A good go-live is quiet. A bad one is felt on the next emergency.

You lead our most complex Logis Dispatch implementations from kickoff to handoff: discovery of how the center works today, configuration, interfaces, data, training, and the cutover itself. You are the senior voice on the team, the one others come to when a project gets hard.

**Where we are headed**

Logis Dispatch is growing across North America and Europe, and into new kinds of customers such as mobile integrated health programs. The product is moving to the cloud and the browser, which will change how fast a center can go live.

You will lead the projects that set the standard, and help design the faster way we will implement next.

**Who ESO is**

ESO is the first responder for the first responders. We build software and data products for EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and government stakeholders, and serve more than 18,000 customers. Our mission is to improve community health and safety outcomes through the power of data.

**How you support the mission**

You support the mission by making sure dispatchers can trust the system in front of them from the first call after cutover. When a center goes live well, crews get to calls faster and leaders can see what is working.

You support your team by setting the standard: you follow the playbook, improve it, and help newer consultants run their first go-lives.

**What you will do**

**Lead each implementation**

* Own a set of Logis Dispatch implementations, including the largest and most complex, each on a dated plan in the project management platform with health, risks, and next steps current every week.

* Run discovery with the center: call types, response plans, units and stations, geography, and the workflows of call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors.

* Raise risks early to your team lead and the customer, with a plan to recover.

**Configure, connect, and cut over**

* Configure Logis Dispatch to the configuration standards, including mapping and unit recommendations.

* Work with Integration Engineering on interfaces: ePCR, billing, mapping and vehicle location, telephony, and paging.

* Plan and run the cutover with the center, often on site, with a rollback plan and a go or no-go call.

**Train, hand off, and raise the bar**

* Train call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and administrators on the workflows they will use every shift.

* Hand off cleanly at go-live: Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care owns tickets, and Customer Success owns the relationship.

* Mentor newer consultants and keep the implementation playbook current with what each project teaches us.

**Time tracking**

* Log your time in real time, as you finish each issue or task, in the time tracking system, by customer and type of work.

**How success is measured**

* Go-lives on the date in the project plan, and right the first time, with no serious incident caused by the setup in the first 30 days.

* Time to value: days from kickoff to the center running live calls in Logis Dispatch, against the standard for the project size.

* Every project plan current each week: dates, health, and next steps.

* Customer satisfaction (CSAT) at go-live and at handoff.

* Clean handoffs: tickets in the first 60 days after go-live go to support, not back to you.

* Time logged in real time and completely, to the team standard.

**Your first** **90 days**

**By day 30.** Systems access; Logis Dispatch configuration standards and the playbook learned; met every customer in your set and taken over each project plan.

**By day 60.** Every project in your set on a current, dated plan. First discovery or configuration milestone delivered to the checklist.

**By day 90.** Owning your full set of implementations, with a cutover planned or delivered, and mentoring at least one newer consultant.

**Dispatch and emergency communications fundamentals**

You bring these on day one, at the depth of someone who has implemented or run a dispatch system:

* How a call moves through a communication center: call-taking, triage, dispatch, unit status, and closing the incident.

* The parts of a dispatch system and what each user does in it: call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and field crews on mobile.

* What connects to the dispatch system and why it matters: ePCR, records management, mapping and vehicle location, radio, telephony, and paging.

* What a bad day looks like on a dispatch floor, and why a slow answer from us is a problem for the people they serve.

**How you grow here**

We grow people through skill badges: short, practical certifications in our products and in the craft of the role. Your badges shape your development plan and open the next role.

* **By day 90:** The Logis Dispatch implementation badges: discovery, configuration standards, interfaces, cutover, and training. Plus the AI working badge: one cutover plan drafted with the assistant and reviewed to standard.

* **By 12 months:** The advanced badges: multi-agency and international projects, recovering a project that has slipped, and certifying new consultants. Plus the validator badge: signing off assistant-drafted project status for your set.

* **Where it leads:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch); Integration Engineering, Logis; or a Success Specialist or CSM role for dispatch customers.

**Tools you will use**

**Tool**

**What you use it for**

  

Project management platform

Every project plan, its dates, health, and next steps

  

Customer relationship management (CRM) system

The handoff from Sales: scope and what was promised

  

Logis Dispatch

Configuration, and the test system for rehearsing the cutover

  

Ticketing system

Escalations during and just after go-live

  

Customer success platform

Account health, shared with Customer Success

  

Team chat

Quick questions and coordination with your team and other teams

  

Time tracking system

Your time by customer and type of work

  

AI workspace and assistants

First drafts of configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates inside the project platform; you review every one.

**What you bring**

**Who does well here**

You will do well here if you have implemented a dispatch system or run one in a communications center, have led live cutovers, and want bigger and more complex projects.

You will also do well if you are a strong implementer ready for the senior seat, and hungry to be the person others come to.

**Required**

* Four or more years implementing dispatch or other public-safety software, or running the system in a 911 or dispatch center.

* You have planned and led a live cutover on a working dispatch floor.

* Comfort with how systems connect: interfaces, mapping, and data moving between systems.

* You run several complex projects at once, and you stay calm and clear with a customer under pressure.

* Able to travel for on-site go-lives.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with Logis Dispatch.

* A dispatcher or telecommunicator background, or EMD or EFD certification.

* Experience with multi-agency, mobile integrated health (MIH), or international dispatch projects.

If you meet most of this and the work excites you, apply. We would rather talk with a strong candidate who took a different path than miss one.

**How the role fits**

**Team and level**

**Implementation, Logis · Senior Implementation Consultant**

  

Reports to

Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch), under the Director of Implementation, Logis

  

Leads

No one; mentors newer consultants

  

Works closely with

Integration Engineering, Logis; Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care; Customer Success, Logis

**How you will use AI**

**Today:** AI helps draft configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates; you review every one.

**Where we are heading:** More of the checking and documenting done by AI, so you spend your time with the center and on the hard configuration questions.

**What stays with you:** The go or no-go call on a cutover, any change to a live dispatch system, and every conversation with a customer about a problem. If an AI assistant drafted it and you signed it, it is yours. You can stop any automated step on your work, and we expect you to when something looks wrong.

**Agents you work with**

Some of your colleagues are software. These are the assistants that draft, check, and flag work for this role today or in the coming year:

* **The project assistant:** Drafts your weekly plan health and flags slipped dates; you confirm before it is published.

* **The Logis knowledge assistant:** Answers configuration and product questions from the product itself; you check the answer before it reaches the center.

* **The capacity engine:** Reads your plans nightly and raises late go-lives and load to the council; the go or no-go call stays yours.

You confirm or correct what they produce before it reaches a customer or a record. Their work counts only when the measures above hold.

**Why ESO**

We build technology for people who run toward emergencies. That sense of purpose runs through how we hire, how we build, and how we show up for our customers. You will work alongside people who care about the communities first responders serve, in a remote, collaborative team that invests in your growth.

**Benefits & Perks**

ESO offers a comprehensive suite of benefits to promote health and financial security for our employees and their families. For full-time employment you this includes:

* Competitive health plans (medical, dental, & vision insurance)
* PTO (starting at 20 days) & 12 company holidays
* 401(k) with company match
* Telemedicine service provided by ESO
* Savings accounts (FSA, HSA, DCA)
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Annual health and wellness reimbursement
* Peace of mind benefits such as life insurance, disability insurance, and worksite benefits
* Paid parental leave, new child program, & flexible parental return-to-work options
* Casual office environments and unlimited office snacks and drinks

**About ESO**

ESO is a fast-paced, growing data, technology, and research company passionate about improving community health and safety through the power of data. We pioneer innovative, user-friendly software to meet the changing needs of today’s EMS agencies, fire departments, and hospitals. We’re small enough to be nimble and fun, but big enough to be a great place to work. We serve thousands of customers out of our offices across the US, Canada and Northern Ireland.

Are you ready to Make a Difference? At ESO, we believe in bringing your true self to work every single day. If you don’t match all the qualifications on the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway! We are looking for passionate, innovative, and authentic people to help drive our mission.

All offers are contingent upon a successful background check.

*ESO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We invite you to consider opportunities at ESO regardless of your gender; gender identity; gender reassignment; age; religion; race; national origin; political affiliation; sexual orientation; disability; veteran status; or other non-merit factor.*

**Customer Onboarding Manager**
===============================

**Location:** Remote, United States

**Experience:** 3–5 years

**About Tessera Labs**
----------------------

Tessera Labs is redefining how enterprises modernize their most complex systems. Backed by Foundation Capital and built by leaders in AI (Artificial Intelligence) and enterprise transformation, Tessera delivers governed, multi-agent AI built specifically for ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) modernization. Tessera compresses ERP modernization from years to weeks.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Customer Onboarding Manager owns every new customer's path from the first handoff by our GTM (Go-To-Market) team to the day the customer is live in production. Your job is to make that path shorter, more predictable, and easier for the customer.

Today, the slowest part of a deal comes after the first sales conversation. Customers need internal approvals before a POC (Proof of Concept) can start: security questionnaires, compliance reviews, infrastructure and architecture questions, and procurement steps. Most of the delay sits on the customer's side, and some sits on ours. You will close both gaps.

You join the customer from the first call, build a shared onboarding plan, and track every open item until it is done. You chase approvals on the customer's side and pull in the right people on ours: GTM, TPM (Technical Project Management), Security, Compliance, and Infrastructure. You do not answer deep technical questions yourself; you make sure the right expert answers them on time.

You will also find the patterns behind the delays and fix them, turning one-off efforts into a repeatable onboarding process.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

**End-to-End Onboarding Ownership**

* Take the handoff from GTM and join customer calls from the start of each engagement.
* Build a shared onboarding plan with each customer covering security review, compliance review, infrastructure questions, procurement, POC, and production go-live.
* Own the timeline, open items, and next steps for several customer onboardings at the same time.
* Keep the customer and internal teams aligned on what is done, what is blocked, and who owns each next step.

**Customer-Side Approvals**

* Map each customer's internal approval path early: who signs off on security, compliance, architecture, legal, and procurement.
* Follow up consistently with customer stakeholders to keep approvals moving.
* Help customers get what their reviewers need, such as completed questionnaires, compliance evidence, and architecture documents.
* Spot stalled approvals early and escalate through the right customer and Tessera contacts.

**Internal Coordination**

* Route customer questions to the right Tessera team (TPM, Security, Compliance, Infrastructure, or GTM) and track them to a committed answer date.
* Make sure handoffs between teams happen without dropped items or repeated questions to the customer.
* Identify internal gaps that slow onboarding, such as missing documents, slow answers, or unclear ownership, and drive fixes with the owning team.

**Process and Reporting**

* Build and maintain a repeatable onboarding playbook, including stage definitions, checklists, templates, and handoff criteria.
* Track onboarding metrics, such as time from GTM handoff to POC start and from POC to production, and report trends to leadership.
* Keep a reusable library of common customer requests and answers with the owning teams so later onboardings move faster.
* Use AI tools to speed up tracking, follow-ups, and reporting.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* 3–5 years of experience in customer onboarding, implementation management, customer success, project coordination, or a similar customer-facing role at a B2B (business-to-business) software company.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, with the confidence to lead calls with customer stakeholders and follow up without being prompted.
* A record of running several customer engagements at once and keeping each one on schedule.
* Experience building processes from scratch, such as playbooks, checklists, and trackers, and getting other teams to use them.
* Strong organization and follow-through, with a habit of clear written status updates.
* Basic understanding of what enterprise security reviews, compliance requirements, and cloud deployments involve. You need to understand the questions well enough to route them; you do not need to answer them.
* Comfort working across teams where you have influence but not direct authority.

**Nice to Have**
----------------

* Experience onboarding enterprise customers through security reviews, vendor due diligence, or procurement at an enterprise SaaS (Software as a Service) or AI company.
* Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 (System and Organization Controls 2) or ISO/IEC 27001 (International Organization for Standardization / International Electrotechnical Commission 27001).
* Exposure to regulated or government customers with long approval cycles.
* Experience with project tracking tools such as Jira, Asana, or a CRM (Customer Relationship Management) system.
* Background at a high-growth startup.

Compensation Range: $150K - $180K

By seamlessly incorporating state-of-the-art AI models into every step of the vehicle photography workflow, we empower businesses to elevate their visual assets at scale, boosting engagement and conversion. We provide a cutting-edge SaaS solution trusted by the industry's top players.

**Trusted by leading automotive brands** and dealer groups across Europe, CarCutter delivers measurable impact where it matters most: helping customers sell more cars, faster, through intelligent automation and data-driven workflows.

CarCutter

**Location: Full-remote in USA, Eastern / Central time are favored**

**Position Overview**
---------------------

**Location:** United States, Full Remote

As an **Onboarding Specialist**, you are the first point of contact for our newly signed customers, guiding them from contract signature to a fully live and successful CarCutter setup. You own the end-to-end onboarding journey, ensuring every dealership, dealer group, or marketplace goes live efficiently, confidently, and with a great experience. Your work directly impacts time-to-value, early adoption, and long-term customer retention.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* **Own the Onboarding Journey:** Manage the full onboarding lifecycle from kickoff call to sanity check completion, ensuring clients go live within defined timelines and with a seamless experience.

* **Progress Tracking:** Maintain accurate and up-to-date onboarding pipeline records in HubSpot, flagging risks, delays, or "ghost" accounts proactively.
* **Issue Resolution:** Serve as the escalation point for onboarding blockers, coordinating with technical teams to resolve integration or configuration issues quickly and effectively.
* **Handoff to Customer Success:** Ensure a smooth and documented transition to the CSM team once the sanity check is validated, sharing key context on customer setup, preferences, and open items.
* **Process Improvement:** Identify recurring friction points in the onboarding process and collaborate with the CX&Ops team to continuously refine playbooks, timelines, and tooling.
* **Ownership**: own a proactive communication with the client by giving as much visibility as possible and be the first defender of costs

---------------------------

* **Experience:** 2+ years of experience in a customer-facing onboarding, implementation, or technical account management role, ideally within a SaaS environment.
* **Industry Knowledge:** Familiarity with the automotive industry or dealership operations is a strong plus.
* **Technical Aptitude:** Comfortable with SaaS integrations, APIs, and web-based tools; ability to understand and explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
* **Project Management Skills:** Proven ability to manage multiple onboarding projects simultaneously, prioritize effectively, and meet deadlines.
* **Communication:** Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to build trust with both technical and business contacts at dealerships and dealer groups.
* **Tool Proficiency:** Experience with CRM tools (HubSpot or similar) and customer success platforms (Arrows).
* **Autonomy:** Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, remote environment while staying aligned with cross-functional teams across time zones.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* A competitive compensation package with a performance-driven structure.
* The opportunity to shape and grow the US onboarding practice from the ground up.
* A collaborative, international team that moves fast and values your impact.

**Hiring Process**
------------------

* Intro call with our Talent Acquisition team.
* Meeting with the Head of Customer Success.
* Meeting with our Partnership manager
* Case study.
* Final conversation with our CRO.
* Reference check.

**—> Up to 78K$ OTE**

jobs.description:
**Assistant Controller, Client Onboarding**
===========================================

Topo is hiring key team members for its accounting team. If you've ever been interested in working at a startup as a member of the initial team, this is it!

Topo provides fractional embedded accounting and finance support to venture-backed companies. Topo's customers look to us as early-stage company experts focused on helping their companies succeed.

We are looking for a strong Assistant Controller to join our Client Onboarding team and help new Topo clients start on a clean, well-built foundation. You'll work hands-on with CEOs and leadership team members at dynamic software and services companies during their first 30–60 days with Topo, getting their books, systems, and processes into shape so they're ready for long-term success.

This position can be remote based in the US. The company is headquartered and based in Indianapolis, Indiana.

**About this role:** Every new Topo client starts with onboarding. In this role, you'll help take clients from signed agreement to fully operational in roughly 30–60 days: assessing their current systems and books, setting them up in Topo's systems, cleaning up historical accounting, and putting sound processes in place before handing them off to the Topo team that will support their accounting on an ongoing basis. We're looking for a high agency person with a strong understanding of and an interest in startups, who enjoys bringing order to messy books and thrives working across several new clients at once. This role will become increasingly strategic as the individual grows within Topo.

**What You'll Do:**

* As the Onboarding Assistant Controller you will kick off new client engagements, gathering system access, documents, and background on the client's business and accounting history.
* Assess each client's current accounting systems, chart of accounts, tech stack, and historical books to identify cleanup needs, gaps, and risks.
* Set up new clients in Topo's systems and tools, including chart of accounts design or restructuring, bank and credit card feeds, and integrations with payroll, billing, and expense platforms.
* Perform historical cleanup, including account reconciliations, catch-up bookkeeping, reclassifications, and adjusting entries, so balances are accurate and supportable.
* Run the client's first month-end closes with Topo, establishing close checklists, reconciliation schedules, and reporting packages, and support initial budget and cash flow setup where in scope.
* Document and implement accounting processes and workflows (e.g., AP, AR, payroll, revenue, and expense management), recommending improvements where needed.
* Coordinate with tax advisors, and prior accountants to obtain records and resolve open items, ensuring timely and accurate completion of deliverables.
* Support and guide Topo team members assisting on onboarding engagements.
* Research technical accounting questions that arise during cleanup and setup, and provide guidance internally and to clients.
* Prepare complete handoff documentation and support a smooth transition to the ongoing Topo accounting team.

**What You'll Need:**

* You're organized and demonstrate a high attention to detail and accuracy.
* You're a self-starter who can put ideas into action.
* You love working with numbers and helping people.
* You enjoy diagnosing and cleaning up messy books, and you take pride in leaving things better than you found them.
* You're comfortable working directly with clients, asking good questions, and setting clear expectations during a period of change.
* You can manage several onboarding engagements at different stages, keep each on track against tight timelines, and write clear documentation others can pick up and run with.
* You have the ability to quickly shift from high-level strategic thinking to tactical execution.
* 4+ years in public accounting, corporate accounting or finance, or similar experience, including month-end close, reconciliations, and cleanup or catch-up accounting.
* Excellent quantitative skills with strong experience in spreadsheet software and familiarity with Quickbooks; experience implementing or migrating accounting systems and integrated tools is a plus.
* Ability to embrace ambiguity, uncertainty, and changing business landscapes.
* CPA strongly preferred.

**What We Value:**
------------------

### **TRUST**

Our team members operate in a high-trust role with customers. Trustworthy team members exhibit: uncompromising integrity, empathy, attention to detail, and the ability to exceed expectations.

### **OWNERSHIP**

Our customers love working with us because we care about the success of their companies as much as they do. Our team members take ownership of the relationship with customers through consistency, responsiveness, and thought partnership.

### **INTELLECTUAL CURIOSITY**

Our customers look to us for guidance on industry standards, recommendations on best practices, and thought leadership. Team members should combine personal experience as well as internal and external resources to be learning machines that will result in strategic insight to the companies we support.

*Topo Advisors is an equal-opportunity employer, and we value diversity at our company. We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.*

*Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.*

**Senior Implementation Consultant, Logis Dispatch**

**Team:** Implementation, Logis · **Level:** Senior Implementation Consultant · **Reports to:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch) · **Location:** Remote, United States

**Outcome.** Dispatch centers go live on Logis Dispatch on the planned date, right the first time, and trust the system from the first call.

**About the role**

A dispatch center cannot stop to go live. When we implement Logis Dispatch, we change the system a center uses to send help to every call, on a floor that runs 24 hours a day. A good go-live is quiet. A bad one is felt on the next emergency.

You lead our most complex Logis Dispatch implementations from kickoff to handoff: discovery of how the center works today, configuration, interfaces, data, training, and the cutover itself. You are the senior voice on the team, the one others come to when a project gets hard.

**Where we are headed**

Logis Dispatch is growing across North America and Europe, and into new kinds of customers such as mobile integrated health programs. The product is moving to the cloud and the browser, which will change how fast a center can go live.

You will lead the projects that set the standard, and help design the faster way we will implement next.

**Who ESO is**

ESO is the first responder for the first responders. We build software and data products for EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and government stakeholders, and serve more than 18,000 customers. Our mission is to improve community health and safety outcomes through the power of data.

**How you support the mission**

You support the mission by making sure dispatchers can trust the system in front of them from the first call after cutover. When a center goes live well, crews get to calls faster and leaders can see what is working.

You support your team by setting the standard: you follow the playbook, improve it, and help newer consultants run their first go-lives.

**What you will do**

**Lead each implementation**

* Own a set of Logis Dispatch implementations, including the largest and most complex, each on a dated plan in the project management platform with health, risks, and next steps current every week.

* Run discovery with the center: call types, response plans, units and stations, geography, and the workflows of call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors.

* Raise risks early to your team lead and the customer, with a plan to recover.

**Configure, connect, and cut over**

* Configure Logis Dispatch to the configuration standards, including mapping and unit recommendations.

* Work with Integration Engineering on interfaces: ePCR, billing, mapping and vehicle location, telephony, and paging.

* Plan and run the cutover with the center, often on site, with a rollback plan and a go or no-go call.

**Train, hand off, and raise the bar**

* Train call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and administrators on the workflows they will use every shift.

* Hand off cleanly at go-live: Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care owns tickets, and Customer Success owns the relationship.

* Mentor newer consultants and keep the implementation playbook current with what each project teaches us.

**Time tracking**

* Log your time in real time, as you finish each issue or task, in the time tracking system, by customer and type of work.

**How success is measured**

* Go-lives on the date in the project plan, and right the first time, with no serious incident caused by the setup in the first 30 days.

* Time to value: days from kickoff to the center running live calls in Logis Dispatch, against the standard for the project size.

* Every project plan current each week: dates, health, and next steps.

* Customer satisfaction (CSAT) at go-live and at handoff.

* Clean handoffs: tickets in the first 60 days after go-live go to support, not back to you.

* Time logged in real time and completely, to the team standard.

**Your first** **90 days**

**By day 30.** Systems access; Logis Dispatch configuration standards and the playbook learned; met every customer in your set and taken over each project plan.

**By day 60.** Every project in your set on a current, dated plan. First discovery or configuration milestone delivered to the checklist.

**By day 90.** Owning your full set of implementations, with a cutover planned or delivered, and mentoring at least one newer consultant.

**Dispatch and emergency communications fundamentals**

You bring these on day one, at the depth of someone who has implemented or run a dispatch system:

* How a call moves through a communication center: call-taking, triage, dispatch, unit status, and closing the incident.

* The parts of a dispatch system and what each user does in it: call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and field crews on mobile.

* What connects to the dispatch system and why it matters: ePCR, records management, mapping and vehicle location, radio, telephony, and paging.

* What a bad day looks like on a dispatch floor, and why a slow answer from us is a problem for the people they serve.

**How you grow here**

We grow people through skill badges: short, practical certifications in our products and in the craft of the role. Your badges shape your development plan and open the next role.

* **By day 90:** The Logis Dispatch implementation badges: discovery, configuration standards, interfaces, cutover, and training. Plus the AI working badge: one cutover plan drafted with the assistant and reviewed to standard.

* **By 12 months:** The advanced badges: multi-agency and international projects, recovering a project that has slipped, and certifying new consultants. Plus the validator badge: signing off assistant-drafted project status for your set.

* **Where it leads:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch); Integration Engineering, Logis; or a Success Specialist or CSM role for dispatch customers.

**Tools you will use**

**Tool**

**What you use it for**

Project management platform

Every project plan, its dates, health, and next steps

Customer relationship management (CRM) system

The handoff from Sales: scope and what was promised

Logis Dispatch

Configuration, and the test system for rehearsing the cutover

Ticketing system

Escalations during and just after go-live

Customer success platform

Account health, shared with Customer Success

Team chat

Quick questions and coordination with your team and other teams

Time tracking system

Your time by customer and type of work

AI workspace and assistants

First drafts of configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates inside the project platform; you review every one.

**What you bring**

**Who does well here**

You will do well here if you have implemented a dispatch system or run one in a communications center, have led live cutovers, and want bigger and more complex projects.

You will also do well if you are a strong implementer ready for the senior seat, and hungry to be the person others come to.

**Required**

* Four or more years implementing dispatch or other public-safety software, or running the system in a 911 or dispatch center.

* You have planned and led a live cutover on a working dispatch floor.

* Comfort with how systems connect: interfaces, mapping, and data moving between systems.

* You run several complex projects at once, and you stay calm and clear with a customer under pressure.

* Able to travel for on-site go-lives.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with Logis Dispatch.

* A dispatcher or telecommunicator background, or EMD or EFD certification.

* Experience with multi-agency, mobile integrated health (MIH), or international dispatch projects.

If you meet most of this and the work excites you, apply. We would rather talk with a strong candidate who took a different path than miss one.

**How the role fits**

**Team and level**

**Implementation, Logis · Senior Implementation Consultant**

Reports to

Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch), under the Director of Implementation, Logis

Leads

No one; mentors newer consultants

Works closely with

Integration Engineering, Logis; Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care; Customer Success, Logis

**How you will use AI**

**Today:** AI helps draft configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates; you review every one.

**Where we are heading:** More of the checking and documenting done by AI, so you spend your time with the center and on the hard configuration questions.

**What stays with you:** The go or no-go call on a cutover, any change to a live dispatch system, and every conversation with a customer about a problem. If an AI assistant drafted it and you signed it, it is yours. You can stop any automated step on your work, and we expect you to when something looks wrong.

**Agents you work with**

Some of your colleagues are software. These are the assistants that draft, check, and flag work for this role today or in the coming year:

* **The project assistant:** Drafts your weekly plan health and flags slipped dates; you confirm before it is published.

* **The Logis knowledge assistant:** Answers configuration and product questions from the product itself; you check the answer before it reaches the center.

* **The capacity engine:** Reads your plans nightly and raises late go-lives and load to the council; the go or no-go call stays yours.

You confirm or correct what they produce before it reaches a customer or a record. Their work counts only when the measures above hold.

**Why ESO**

We build technology for people who run toward emergencies. That sense of purpose runs through how we hire, how we build, and how we show up for our customers. You will work alongside people who care about the communities first responders serve, in a remote, collaborative team that invests in your growth.

**About ESO**

ESO is a fast-paced, growing data, technology, and research company passionate about improving community health and safety through the power of data. We pioneer innovative, user-friendly software to meet the changing needs of today's EMS agencies, fire departments, and hospitals. We're small enough to be nimble and fun, but big enough to be a great place to work. We serve thousands of customers out of our offices across the US, Canada and Northern Ireland.

Are you ready to Make a Difference? At ESO, we believe in bringing your true self to work every single day. If you don't match all the qualifications on the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway! We are looking for passionate, innovative, and authentic people to help drive our mission.
